physical.location: Inside the coin door
physical.notes: The Self-Test button inside the coin door (manual Figure 1), wired from A4J3-1 (R) to A3J2-7 (Y-R) on the cabinet sheet. Public -7 drives the ROM's tests in the manual's order: in the retained runs the first press starts the burn-in, the fourth the solenoid test and the fifth the switch test.

physical.location: MPU module
physical.notes: PinMAME routes public -6 to the CPU's NMI line (BY35_SWCPUDIAG). The manual names no button for it; the S33 MEMORY CLEAR pushbuttons are a separate contact (the remote memory-clear input), so the identity of the two is not assumed.

physical.location: Sound module
physical.notes: PinMAME routes public -5 to the ST300 sound board's diagnostic input (BY35_SWSOUNDDIAG). The manual documents no such button on the B-605 sound board.

physical.location: Coin door and cabinet
physical.notes: Switch Identification table: `CHUTE`; matrix sheet: `CHUTE`. Normally open contact with a series 1N4004 diode on the cabinet sheet. SW-1 of the coin-door drawing on the Switch Identification page: the middle chute of the US three-chute door (the German door puts SW-1 at the hinge). The location page lists it as `1 * LEFT CHUTE` and refers to that drawing. Cabinet sheet return A4J3-9, printed `(R-W)`; the credit tables call switch 1 `WIRE COLOR BLUE` and switch 3 `RED-WHITE`, the reverse of the cabinet sheet's colours for returns A4J3-9 and A4J3-11, a wire-colour disagreement that does not change the address. A coin on it adds one credit in the retained gameplay run.

physical.notes: Switch Identification table: `SPIN-TARGET (LEFT)`; matrix sheet: `SP.T. (LEFT)`. Normally open contact with a series 1N4004 diode on the playfield wiring diagram. The manual: the left spinner lites when X is lit; it scored 2,000 per closure in the retained gameplay run while card X was selected. Placed on the retained table's Spinner `sw4`, which its script binds to this address.

physical.notes: Switch Identification table: `TILTS`; matrix sheet: `TILT`. Normally open contact with a series 1N4004 diode on the cabinet sheet. Shared matrix position for two normally open tilt contacts: the location page lists `7 ROLL-TILT` and `7 PENDULUM`, and the cabinet sheet draws two contacts in parallel on return A4J3-15 (BLU-O) with a capacitor across them. The installation page counts three normally open tilt switches (plumb bob, ball tilt and a panel tilt on the bottom of the playfield panel); the location page puts the tilt board on 8, so the panel tilt is not counted here. Closing public 7 in play drops the flipper-enable output 19 and lights TILT (lamp 61) in the retained gameplay run.

physical.location: Coin door and cabinet
physical.notes: Switch Identification table: `SLAM & VIB. TILTS`; matrix sheet: `SLAM`. Normally open contact with a series 1N4004 diode on the cabinet sheet. Shared matrix position for the slam contacts. The location page lists `8 TILT BOARD` and `8 DOOR & PLAYFIELD VIB.`; the operating text says there is a slam switch on the front door, one on the tilt board and one on the playfield, and that an operator may fit more. The cabinet sheet draws one SLAM contact on return A4J3-16 (Y). Because operators may add contacts, no quantity is asserted. In the retained slam run, closing public 8 in play ends the game and the ROM repeats its power-up initialisation.

mechanisms.behavior: Big Game is a single-ball machine with no trough. The known-working scripts start with the ball on the out-hole switch (public 33). When the credit button starts a game the ROM resets the three drop banks (public 7, 8 and 9) and kicks the out-hole (public 11, J-26-1000), repeating the kick and the bank resets for as long as public 33 stays closed; the retained runs show the repeats stop once 33 opens. The kick sends the ball to the shooter lane, where the player launches it with the plunger. After every drain the bonus is counted, the player and ball advance, and the kick repeats; an extra ball is played without advancing (manual).
mechanisms.label: Single-ball out-hole and shooter feed

mechanisms.behavior: A saucer at the top of the left loop (parts list `Saucer Eject` J-28-2300). A ball in it holds public 34 closed and the ROM answers with a pulse on public 10 that ejects it back into the loop (retained gameplay run). The pocket scores 5,000 for each lit letter of B-I-G-G-A-M-E and 35,000 more when the word is made (manual). The known-working scripts eject at 55 degrees with force 20.
mechanisms.label: Top eject pocket (saucer)

mechanisms.behavior: Three drop targets printed 3, 2, 1 from top to bottom on the bank (switches 14, 15, 16), angled below the top-left roll-over button. A target's switch is closed while it is down; one reset coil (public 7, B-27-2300) raises the whole bank and there is no individual knock-down coil. Home state is all three up. The ROM resets the bank at game start and after every drain, and again when the bank's last target goes down (retained gameplay run: public 7 fires on the third closure). Each target scores 500 and spots its number in the selected card or cards (manual and retained run); once a bank's numbers are spotted on all three cards, each further completion scores 25,000 (manual).
mechanisms.label: Top left three-target drop bank (1A)

mechanisms.behavior: Three drop targets printed 4, 5, 6 from top to bottom (switches 24, 23, 22), angled below the right roll-over lane. A target's switch is closed while it is down; one reset coil (public 8, B-27-2300) raises the whole bank and there is no individual knock-down coil. Home state is all three up. The ROM resets the bank at game start and after every drain, and again when the bank's last target goes down (retained gameplay run: public 8 fires on the third closure). Each target scores 500 and spots its number in the selected card or cards (manual and retained run); once a bank's numbers are spotted on all three cards, each further completion scores 25,000 (manual).
mechanisms.label: Top right three-target drop bank (1B)

mechanisms.behavior: Three drop targets printed 7, 8, 9 from top to bottom (switches 32, 31, 30) along the right side above the right return lane. A target's switch is closed while it is down; one reset coil (public 9, B-27-2300) raises the whole bank and there is no individual knock-down coil. Home state is all three up. The ROM resets the bank at game start and after every drain, and again when the bank's last target goes down (retained gameplay run: public 9 fires on the third closure). Each target scores 500 and spots its number in the selected card or cards (manual and retained run); once a bank's numbers are spotted on all three cards, each further completion scores 25,000 (manual).
mechanisms.label: Lower right three-target drop bank (1C)

mechanisms.behavior: Two spin target assemblies (A-563-11, target and wire 14A-7-10) hang on one wire across the left loop, left spinner (switch 4) at the outer end and right spinner (switch 5) beside the top-left drop bank. Each rotation closes its contact once; there is no coil or home sensor. The left spinner's value is lit with card X and the right one's when B-I-G is made (manual; lamps 37 and 30).
mechanisms.label: Two spinning targets across the left loop

mechanisms.behavior: Three J-26-1200 thumper bumpers. The ROM fires each coil when its own switch closes and scores 1,000 on the 3-ball setting (100 on 5-ball, manual): switch 9 (top) fires public 1, switch 10 (lower left) public 2 and switch 11 (lower right) public 3 in the retained gameplay run. The top bumper also changes the card selection. Printed solenoid numbers are 2, 1 and 5.
mechanisms.label: Three thumper bumpers

mechanisms.behavior: Two J-27-1500 slingshots. The ROM fires each coil when its switch closes, scores 10 and changes the card selection: switch 12 fires public 4 and switch 13 public 5 (retained gameplay run). Printed solenoid numbers are 6 and 7.
mechanisms.label: Left and right slingshots

mechanisms.behavior: Two flippers on each side, one above the other at the bottom of the playfield (playfield-parts drawing; IPDB `Flippers (4)`). Each side's lower (J-25-475/34-4500) and upper (J-25-500/34-5050) coils are wired in parallel on one drive wire (right A3J1-9, left A3J1-8) from the +43 VDC supply A2J1-6, through the contacts of the flipper enable relay to the side's single cabinet button (right A3J2-1, left A3J2-2). The relay is public 19 (printed solenoid 15): the ROM raises it when a game starts and drops it on a tilt and at game over (retained runs). Each coil's end-of-stroke contact is closed at rest and opens at the end of the stroke to insert the hold winding. PinMAME publishes one callback per side (46 right, 48 left, with 45 and 47 alongside), so a recreation moves both flippers of a side together.
mechanisms.label: Four dual-winding flippers, two per button

mechanisms.behavior: Two one-way ball gates with no coil or switch: `BALL GATE ASS'Y. A-104-R2` at the top of the right lane and `LEFT GATE ASS'Y. A-104-L` at the top of the left loop (playfield-parts drawing). They route the ball by its own motion; do not invent a powered diverter.

ILLUM` straight from A2J1-8 (6 VAC) to A2J1-1, and the transformer and wiring sheets take the backbox general illumination straight from the transformer. physical.notes: PinMAME's synthetic power-winding state for the right side, asserted and released together with public 46 for the whole enabled button closure (retained gameplay run). It is not another coil and does not measure the power winding.

The two right flippers (parts list `Flipper Lower L & R` J-25-475/34-4500 and `Flipper Upper L & R` J-25-500/34-5050) are dual-winding coils wired in parallel on one drive wire, hard-wired from the +43 VDC supply A2J1-6 (BLU-W) through the flipper enable relay's contacts to the right cabinet button; no numbered solenoid transistor drives them. Placed on the retained table's two right flipper pivots (`RightFlipper` lower, `RightFlipper1` upper), both moved by this callback.
